- Catalyst order: If rate ∝ [cat] (M1) vs [cat]² dimerization (M3) or dimer deactivation (M13), varying [cat] will separate them.

- Product inhibition (M12, M17) - test by adding product.

For the second experiment, use HIGH substrate + LOW catalyst. This amplifies effects of deactivation (M9/M11/M13/M14/M19/M20 will fail to reach full conversion), and helps expose substrate inhibition (M11, M16). Also, the effect of catalyst dimerization (M2, M3, M13) is more pronounced at higher catalyst - so I'll actually contrast that later. 

For now, high substrate = 3.0 M, low catalyst = 0.005 M, no product. This is complementary: long timescale, potential deactivation visible; if substrate inhibition (M11/M16), rate will be depressed unusually; if pure MM (M1), simple saturation kinetics.
</hypothesis>
